$comment: The iOS launch-screen device table. ONE source, TWO consumers:
`scripts/generate-splash.mjs` rasterises a PNG per row, and `src/app/layout.tsx`
emits an `apple-touch-startup-image` link tag per row.
⚠️ This file exists because the two halves CANNOT be allowed to drift. iOS picks
a splash by matching the media query exactly; a tag with no file shows a white
screen, and a file with no tag is dead weight nobody notices. Hand-keeping a list
of tags beside a list of files is the same failure `scripts/generate-icons.mjs`
was written to prevent, and the one that drifts is always the size the phone in
your pocket actually renders. `splash.test.ts` asserts the two stay in step.
Portrait only, deliberately: the app is a phone-form-factor product with no
landscape layout, and iOS falls back to the app's background colour when no
orientation matches — which, on this floor, is the right fallback anyway.
`width`/`height` are CSS points (what the media query matches); the raster is
width x ratio by height x ratio. Ordered newest-first so the models most likely
to be in use sit at the top of the head.
